eyebrow: NSGs that enforce the tier boundary
code:
az network nsg rule create --nsg-name web-nsg \
  --name Allow-Web --priority 100 --access Allow \
  --protocol Tcp --destination-port-ranges 80 443 \
  --source-address-prefixes Internet

az network nsg rule create --nsg-name app-nsg \
  --name Allow-From-Web --priority 100 --access Allow \
  --protocol Tcp --destination-port-ranges 8080 \
  --source-address-prefixes 10.20.1.0/24
caption: The app subnet only trusts traffic already inside the web subnet — not the internet.

eyebrow: RBAC, scoped to the resource group
code:
az role assignment create \
  --assignee-object-id <briarcliff-ops-group-id> \
  --assignee-principal-type Group \
  --role "Virtual Machine Contributor" \
  --scope "/subscriptions/<sub-id>/resourceGroups/briarcliff-rg"
caption: The ops team gets VM management rights on this resource group — not the subscription.

code:
az monitor action-group create --name ops-email-ag \
  --short-name opsAG \
  --email-receivers name=OpsTeam email=ops@briarcliffsystems.com

az monitor metrics alert create --name high-cpu-web-vm1 \
  --scopes <web-vm1-resource-id> \
  --condition "avg Percentage CPU > 80" \
  --window-size 5m --action ops-email-ag

az consumption budget create --budget-name briarcliff-monthly-budget \
  --amount 150 --resource-group briarcliff-rg --time-grain Monthly
caption: One alert watches CPU, the other watches the bill — both email the same ops team.
